A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distribution-classification research despite the revised title and expanded scope. Text extraction and visual inspection cover all 18 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including appendices, and support matching equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original distribution-classification experiments, a human study, and crop, frequency, and pretraining analyses in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds same-distribution controls, GAN detection, self-supervised text-to-image results, and downstream training experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed distribution-classification procedure, supervised and self-supervised classifier approaches, and default rectangular filtering remain unchanged. The new theoretical explanation and additional evaluation applications do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: The real datasets remain CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and COCO2014. However, Section 7.2 adds supervised and semi-supervised semantic classification using real and EDM-generated training data, substantially extending the task coverage beyond source-distribution classification and human judgments.

E2.justification: The new downstream comparison includes FlexMatch, FreeMatch, and DPT/FreeMatch augmentation attributed to You et al. (Table 8). MAE and MoCo v3 also join the text-to-image evaluation (Table 15), whereas v1 evaluated them only on label-to-image combinations. The original supervised classifier comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces same-distribution controls, circular-filter testing, and replacement-versus-augmentation protocols varying the synthetic-data ratio, with four labels per class in the semi-supervised comparison. The reported human-study sample increases from 11 to 19 participants. Existing core training settings in Appendices A and B remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds checks of same-distribution distinguishability, rectangular versus circular filtering, and sensitivity to synthetic-data replacement or augmentation. Figure 11 also extends frequency analysis to StyleGAN-XL. Conversely, v1's Grad-CAM analysis and Figure 4 are removed. Existing crop, pretraining, and within-EDM2 frequency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 gains standard-deviation error bars across participants and classifier performances; v1 showed point summaries and explicitly used median classifier accuracy. The existing four-trial crop uncertainty reporting remains unchanged. An increase in repeated training runs or seeds is not documented.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results as v2 Tables 2–7. New results include same-distribution accuracy of 50.14–50.83% (Table 1), StyleGAN-XL detection accuracy of 96.85–99.95% (Table 14), self-supervised text-to-image scores (Table 15), and replacement/augmentation and filter-comparison outcomes (Figures 6 and 11; Table 8). Figure 3 summaries also change with the expanded participant sample and revised statistical presentation.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces a formal connection between binary classification and distribution divergence through the cross-entropy objective, optimal density-ratio classifier, and JSD argument (Equations 5–7). v1 has no corresponding derivation. However, Equation 7 reverses the signs required by the negative cross-entropy loss defined in Equation 5.

C1.justification: The central distinguishability and classifier-versus-FID findings remain. However, v2 removes the prominent claim that classifiers primarily rely on edges and elevates complementary generator diagnosis, an explanation of Model Autophagy Disorder, and the superiority of augmentation over replacement into main contributions in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: Retained spatial and frequency findings are reinterpreted as diagnosing which features diffusion models learn successfully. v2 adds distribution-mismatch explanations for model collapse and downstream degradation, discussion of FID's assumptions, and an explanation involving fixed versus evolving GAN distributions. The MAD explanation is not supported by a new recursive-training experiment. v1's explicit dataset/architecture generalizability qualification disappears.

D1.justification: Appendix C.6 newly documents participant expertise, ages, vision, displays, zooming, duration, and compensation. A reproducibility statement says PyTorch code and README instructions accompany the submission, although their availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing hyperparameters, hardware costs, and external code-link tables are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around synthetic-data training, model collapse, and limitations of FID, adding connections to Alemohammad et al., Shumailov et al., You et al., and Kynkäänniemi et al. Related work more explicitly distinguishes generator diagnosis from detection performance. The Grad-CAM citation and several background references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusions are extensively rewritten. Section 6's separate subsections are consolidated and reordered, while Section 7 reorganizes the existing spatial/frequency narrative around implications. The title and affiliation text change, and ethics and reproducibility statements are introduced.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for controls, downstream learning, GAN detection, and self-supervised text-to-image evaluation, plus downstream and filter-comparison figures. Figure 3 is redrawn with error bars, and the Grad-CAM figure is removed. Retained frequency figures are renumbered, while the document template, typography, and figure/table placement change substantially.

improvement.justification: Same-distribution controls, filter-shape checks, and a larger human study with uncertainty reporting strengthen validation, while downstream experiments add practical evidence. However, new Appendix D contains a sign error in its central divergence equation, and the expanded model-collapse claim lacks direct recursive-training evidence. These benefits and weaknesses in the newly emphasized scientific arguments prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
